description: Governing policies for the Jarvis Improvement Loop (JIL). Machine-checkable rules that constrain every loop turn regardless of goal. Mirrored into .jarvis/memory/loop/ for cross-session continuity.

grounding_policy.statement: Before the first Discover, the loop MUST ground its grading rubric in external evidence (repo first, then trusted web/KB). Every criterion that enters the gate must cite a source and be checkable. A criterion with no source is marked 'unverifiable' and escalated to the user — it never enters the gate, and the loop never grades against an ungrounded criterion.
rejects_turn_when: work began before a locked rubric exists
a criterion was graded without a cited source
the LLM both authored and graded a criterion with no external anchor

loop_contract.statement: A turn is complete only when all six phases are done and cited: Ground (once, up front) -> Discover -> Hypothesis -> Implement -> Verify -> Next-direction. Discover must cite real probed state. Verify must run the locked gate (deterministic-first) and prove the change. One real change per turn — no batched cosmetic edits.
rejects_turn_when: Discover skipped or not cited with real evidence
Verify skipped, or the gate was not actually run
change was cosmetic with no measurable result
more than one substantive change bundled without individual verification

plateau_policy.statement: If no criterion is failing and no further change produces a measurable, sourced improvement, record ONE plateau note (with evidence) and stop. Never pad turns or manufacture busywork to appear productive.
rejects_turn_when: a turn ran after a genuine plateau was reached
a turn produced no measurable progress and was not recorded as plateau

human_gate_policy.statement: Pause and ask for explicit human approval before any irreversible or shared-world action. The loop proposes; a human applies. Default autonomy is propose-only.
requires_human_approval: applying a skill/agent/starter/scenario edit to main (self-improvement is staged as a candidate, never auto-applied)
git push, force-push, branch/file deletion, or history rewrite
writing to a real (non-sandbox) Figma file or sending any message/notification
any credential, recruiter, or external-publish action
human_gate_policy.sandbox_exception: Autonomous iteration is allowed WITHOUT prompting only inside a sandbox: a scratch git branch or a projects/<slug>/ working copy, where every action is reversible and the deterministic gate stays green.

rejection_criteria.description: A loop turn is REJECTED (not counted as genuine) if any of these hold.
rules: grades against a criterion with no cited source
makes a cosmetic change with no measurable, sourced result
pads turns after a real plateau
auto-applies a self-improvement edit to main, edits a baseline file, or performs a human-gated action without approval
